# Python SDK & CLI

The `windborne` package provides both a Python library and a CLI for interacting with the Data and Forecast APIs.

## Installation

pip3 install windbornepip3 install windborne

Show MoreShow Less

* * *

## Set Credentials

The SDK reads `WB_API_KEY` from an environment variable.

### macOS & Linux

\# Add to your shell config (~/.bashrc, ~/.zshrc, etc.)\# Add to your shell config (~/.bashrc, ~/.zshrc, etc.)

export WB\_API\_KEY='$WB\_API\_KEY
[Log in to see API keys](https://api.windbornesystems.com/docs-auth/start?return_to=%2Fplatform%2Fintegrations%2Fpython-sdk%2F)
'export WB\_API\_KEY='$WB\_API\_KEY
[Log in to see API keys](https://api.windbornesystems.com/docs-auth/start?return_to=%2Fplatform%2Fintegrations%2Fpython-sdk%2F)
'

\# Reload your shell or run:\# Reload your shell or run:

source ~/.zshrcsource ~/.zshrc

Show MoreShow Less

### Windows

1. Press Win + X and select "System"
2. Click "Advanced system settings" on the right
3. Click "Environment Variables" at the bottom
4. Under "User variables", click "New" and add:

| Variable Name | Variable Value |
| WB\_API\_KEY | your\_api\_key |

## CLI Usage

After installation, the `windborne` command is available globally.

\# Fetch observations\# Fetch observations

windborne observations2026-11-09T19:33:44Z2026-11-10T01:33:44Z observations.csvwindborne observations2026-11-09T19:33:44Z2026-11-10T01:33:44Z observations.csv

\# Get a dynamic point forecast\# Get a dynamic point forecast

windborne points\_interpolated 37.7749,-122.4194 -m wm-6 --min-time2026-11-10T22:33:44Z --max-time2026-11-11T01:33:44Zwindborne points\_interpolated 37.7749,-122.4194 -m wm-6 --min-time2026-11-10T22:33:44Z --max-time2026-11-11T01:33:44Z

\# List flying missions\# List flying missions

windborne flying\_missions output.jsonwindborne flying\_missions output.json

## Python Library

from windborne import get\_observations, get\_point\_forecasts\_interpolatedfrom windborne import get\_observations, get\_point\_forecasts\_interpolated

\# Fetch observations\# Fetch observations

observations = get\_observations(observations = get\_observations(

start\_time="2026-11-09T19:33:44Z", start\_time="2026-11-09T19:33:44Z",

end\_time="2026-11-10T01:33:44Z", end\_time="2026-11-10T01:33:44Z",

output\_file="observations.csv" output\_file="observations.csv"

))

\# Get a dynamic point forecast\# Get a dynamic point forecast

forecast = get\_point\_forecasts\_interpolated(forecast = get\_point\_forecasts\_interpolated(

coordinates=\[(37.7749, -122.4194)\], coordinates=\[(37.7749, -122.4194)\],

model="wm-6", model="wm-6",

min\_forecast\_time="2026-11-10T22:33:44Z", min\_forecast\_time="2026-11-10T22:33:44Z",

max\_forecast\_time="2026-11-11T01:33:44Z", max\_forecast\_time="2026-11-11T01:33:44Z",

print\_response=True print\_response=True

))
